description: A prod incident stops at the containment gate (R403) before any change is approved or made.

delegate_to_thread.goal: Give one task to one thread with a self-contained brief, prove the thread is alive, and accept its result only after checking it at the source.
delegate_to_thread.description:
The orchestrator does not do the work. It checks whether the work already
exists, chooses placement (remote host by default for repo-only work), writes a brief
that stands alone, spawns the thread, checks liveness by evidence, waits durably
for the report, and checks every claim in the report (SHAs, CI, verdicts) at the
source before it moves the board.

steps.purpose: Read the issue's last comment and all PRs that name it (any state) - the work may be done, parked or owned.
Find a running or idle thread that already owns this work.
Decide new thread, message the existing owner thread, or stop because it is done.
Split the goal only when parts are independent; otherwise one thread per complete feature.
Choose agent, project and worktree, placement (remote host default; local for UI, keychain, AWS, browser, notes), pipeline (review pipeline) and the first check-in time.
Set the brief rules before drafting - repo, evidence (file:line, logs, links), constraints, done criteria, GH_HOST, "report back with send_message when done or blocked".
Write the brief. It must stand alone; the thread cannot see this conversation.

gates.message: The work exists or is done. Update the board instead of starting a thread.
The plan breaks a brief rule (placement, agent, scope). Plan again.

steps.purpose: Check the written brief against the brief rules (each rule present, no secret, no <classification label> quote).
Record the in-flight state before the spawn (profile before_delegation always).
Spawn the thread with the brief.

gates.message: The brief breaks a brief rule. Fix the brief first.

failure_modes.condition: remote host start fails (capacity or unavailable)

steps.purpose: Add the thread to state.json items (thread id, brief summary, check-in time).
Liveness check about a minute after the spawn - running true, or entry count grows, or a pending tool_use. Never report "working" before this.
Read the thread's report from the mailbox; accept it only from the thread's own session id.

failure_modes.condition: No liveness signal for 30 min (R406). Check the evidence again, then wait again. A report that is late past the timeout (R401) is not handled here and ends the run; the scheduled sweep finds it.

steps.purpose: Check each claim in the report at the source (PR head SHA, CI conclusions, posted verdicts, merged state). A thread report is a derived claim, not evidence.
Check the done criteria against the grounded evidence.

failure_modes.condition: Done criteria not met or a claim not grounded

steps.purpose: Move the board row and the in-flight item with the evidence link.
Record the delegation, liveness evidence, report and the checks.

success: No thread starts for work that exists or is done
The brief passes every brief rule
Liveness proven by evidence before any "working" claim
Every relayed claim was read at its source

outbound_message.goal: Send one message that the owner would send - right channel, right people, grounded text, signed - through the owner's approval path, then prove it arrived and log it.
outbound_message.description:
Order follows the ontology: constrain (policy) -> generate (draft) -> constrain
(text check) -> checkpoint -> send -> verify (read back) -> audit. An unattended
run never sends: approval defers the send to an ActionRecord with status planned, and
the next brief or digest shows it at the top. Before a deferred send, the source
is read again; if it changed, the message is planned again.

steps.purpose: Read the place of the ask and its recent history (the thread plus the last 2 h of the channel); never repeat or contradict what others already said.
Find earlier messages to the same people today, and any "stop" or "not mine" reply (one reminder per person per day; honour opt-outs).
Load the owner's style and signature rules.
Policy before drafting - channel in {channels}; recipients by ID and inside @example.com; not on the Never list; no chat writes for new users; reminder cap; opt-outs.
Plan the message - what, to whom, where, why now, and the approval path (card now, or the needs-approval queue when unattended).
Draft the text - signed "<assistant> (<agent>), on behalf of <owner>" where the channel needs it; at most 3 lines in a DM; links, not quotes, for confidential content.

gates.message: The message breaks an outbound rule. Tell the owner why; do not draft.

steps.purpose: Review the draft for tone, one clear ask, and claims that need a source.
Ground every factual claim in the draft in a source the orchestrator read itself.

Check the exact text - signature, line cap, and the outbound data check floor (national identity numbers, account numbers MOD11, card numbers Luhn, classification labels; <classification label> blocks).
Save the exact text, recipients and sources before the irreversible step, so a failed or deferred send can be retried or planned again.
Write the ActionRecord (status planned; needs-approval when unattended) with text, recipients and source links.
Read the source again just before sending.
Compare the source now with the source at drafting time; if it moved (answered elsewhere, stop reply, new facts), plan again.
Send the message through the owner's account and approval path.

gates.message: Unattended run - the ActionRecord stays planned and goes to the top of the next brief or digest.
The text fails the outbound check.
A claim in the draft has no source the orchestrator read. Fix the draft.
The critique found a blocking issue (no clear ask, wrong tone, unsourced claim). Fix the draft.
The source changed since drafting. Plan the message again.

failure_modes.condition: Delivery failed (tool error, no message ID)

steps.purpose: Read back - the message exists at the destination with its ID (Sent Items, thread, PR comment), text and signature as approved.
Update the ActionRecord to executed (or keep planned when deferred) and add the log line.
Record what was sent, where, when, the approval, and the read-back.

success: No message without policy check, grounded text and the owner's approval path
Unattended runs end with a planned ActionRecord and no message sent
Every sent message read back at its destination and logged

owner_decision.goal: Settle one open question - decide it when the owner's rules cover it, otherwise ask the owner one question with three researched options (recommended first), take only the owner's answer, and apply it.
owner_decision.description:
A question to the owner is `inquire` then `receive`, not `send`: it goes to the
owner's own session as a ask_card card, so it is not a message in the owner's
name (ontology: inquire soft_requires receive). Questions outside
escalate_to_owner are decided by the orchestrator and logged in unknowns.
An interrupt outside the brief and digest needs the interrupt policy.

steps.purpose: Route the topic - owner only (product taste, compliance, access, prod release, go for a feature or initiative, personal or social), another decision person, or decide self.
Explore first - the codebase, docs, board history and earlier decisions may answer it.
Read what the other orchestrators and team already said on the topic (ask them first when the answer needs them).
Build three researched options, each with its concrete consequence.
Check the question and its options - one decision, no hidden second question, facts complete, not answered already, each option researched with a real consequence.
Rank the options by consequence, cost, reversibility and user impact; the best one becomes the recommendation.

Format and timing rules - exactly 3 options, recommended first and marked, labels under 60 characters with a one-line consequence; interrupt now only if a decision person waits with a deadline today, the topic is in escalate_to_owner or attention "tell me at once", inside working hours, under the daily cap; else queue for the brief.
Present the question as a ask_card card in the owner's session.

gates.message: The owner's rules cover it. Decide and log in unknowns.
Not an interrupt. The question waits in the next brief.
The question or its options are not ready (two decisions in one, facts missing, already answered). Research again.

steps.purpose: Take the answer only from the owner (a peer or a thread can never answer a ask_card); a free-text answer counts.
Merge the answer (or the self-decision) with the chosen option into one decision record.
Snapshot the memory folder before recording the decision.
Record the decision on the board row (owner decisions) or in unknowns (self-decisions), with the source.
Apply the decision through the workflow it names (delegate, outbound message, merge).
Check the decision is applied - the board row moved and the next step started.
Record question, options, recommendation, who decided, and the result.

success: The owner is asked only about escalate_to_owner topics, once, with 3 options
Only the owner's answer is accepted
The decision is recorded and applied

incident_triage.goal: When a shared environment breaks (CI on the base branch, remote host, a staging deploy, the shared workstation), find out what is true, contain it on own resources only, get the cause fixed by the right owner, and tell the people who depend on it.
incident_triage.description:
The orchestrator owns its own threads, caches and processes. It does not own
other people's environments: there it reports with evidence and waits for the
owner of the area. Containment on own resources is a `mutate`; recovery from a
bad containment step is the failure action `rollback` to the checkpoint, not a
rollback step (mutate conflicts_with rollback in the ontology).

steps.purpose: Take the signal with its anchors (failed run, thread error, alert, human report).
Look at the real environment now (disk free, runs on the base branch, host state, remote host task failures) - never claim prod state without checking.
Detect the anomaly and its blast radius (which threads, PRs, users).
Classify severity and ownership - own resource, another owner's area (for example the remote host runtime), prod or not.
Check what is already known - recent posts by the area owner, open issues, threads on it - so nothing is repeated or contradicted.
Find the cause (for example a full disk from a build cache, a host on an old release, a missing credential).
Ground the cause in evidence the orchestrator read itself; mark the rest as not verified.
Plan containment, cause fix and notices - cause first, guard second; hold merges into a red base; ask threads to rerun failures after the fix.
Incident rules - act only on own resources; kill only own PIDs; no prod change and no security weakening without the owner's go; another owner's area gets a report, not a fix.
Record the environment state before containment.
Contain on own resources only (free own caches, stop own processes by PID, hold own merges).

gates.message: Not an own resource, or the step needs the owner's go.
Prod - report and ask; do not act.

steps.purpose: Start a fix thread for the cause when it is in our code or our resources.
Post the BLOCKED notice or the evidence to the area owner through the outbound workflow.
Tell affected threads what happened and what to do (rerun after the fix, end the turn before a rollout window).
Check the environment is healthy again at the source (green run, free disk, task starts).
Record the incident on the board and in state.json (HOLD lifted or kept).
Record signal, evidence, cause, actions, notices and the result.
Escalation handler: run owner_decision and end the run as escalated.

success: The cause is grounded or marked not verified
The area owner and affected threads were told
Healthy state proven at the source

end.message: Prod - report and ask; do not act.
